messages.subject: Bubble chart size and colour
parts:
Dear list,

I've succesfully plotted a bubble chart for my restaurant data set. My
"info" dataframe consists of longitude / latitude / rating

My ratings continuous values, but for now I've rounded them off to be
discrete values. My problem is the following. I'd like to use 10 fixed
colours for depicting the ratings. The ratings are between 0 and 10.
Moreover, I'd like the points to scale proportionally to their rating.
This allows me to compare the ratings of the restaurants by looking at
the legend for both the point size and colour. I've struggled with the
aesthetics, but couldn't get it right. My code is as follows. How can
I make sure that let's say, the 10 colours are rainbow(10) AND have
the size depend on the rating?

Kind regards,

Michel

library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)

lng <- c
(4.482566,4.473565,4.483039,4.474304,4.485887,4.474615,4.497905,4.476821,4.476111,4.481135,4.491674,4.482028,4.483648,4.504239,4.51775,4.517735,4.510746,4.517979,4.477751,4.478252,4.47903,4.479929,4.471585,4.47866,4.478029,4.523455,4.490437,4.486032,4.488442)

lat <- c
(51.913126,51.915905,51.91792,51.916159,51.915666,51.91442,51.921744,51.915445,51.916552,51.916185,51.918877,51.918925,51.91889,51.921842,51.916974,51.916979,51.920805,51.918007,51.909958,51.909476,51.908888,51.909112,51.903885,51.909551,51.906958,51.895308,51.907031,51.901382,51.88934)

rating <- c
(8.0,8.0,8.0,8.0,0.0,9.0,8.0,8.0,9.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,7.0,8.0,9.0,9.0,0.0,8.0,8.0,8.0,7.0,7.0,9.0,8.0,7.0,0.0,6.0,7.0,7.0)

info <- data.frame(lng, lat, rating)

no_margins <- opts(
legend.background = theme_rect(fill = "white", col= "white", size =
4),
legend.position = c(0.9, 0.5),
axis.line = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_blank(),
axis.text.y = theme_blank(),
axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
axis.title.x = theme_blank(),
axis.title.y = theme_blank(),
axis.ticks.length = unit(0, "cm"),
axis.ticks.margin = unit(0, "cm"),

panel.background = theme_blank(),
panel.border = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.major = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(),

plot.background = theme_blank(),
plot.title = theme_blank(),
plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "lines")
)

myplot <- ggplot(data = info, aes(lng, lat)) +
geom_point(aes(size=rating), colour=alpha(rainbow(29), 0.7)) +
scale_size(name='Ratings', limit=c(0, 10), breaks=1:10, to = c(0, 15))
+
coord_cartesian(xlim=c(4.472637176513672, 4.527568817138672), ylim=c
(51.878928367413394, 51.92976563010761)) +
no_margins

Cairo(file="plot.png", type='png', bg='transparent', width=320,
height=480)
print(myplot)

messages.subject: Re: Bubble chart size and colour
parts:
Hi Michel,

You need to do the same thing you did with size: map colour to
rating, and then find an appropriate scale that performs the mapping
that you want. In this case, I'd say you want scale_gradientn which
allows to you create a mapping to any continuous colour gradient:

geom_point(aes(size=rating, colour = rating)) +
scale_size(name='Ratings', limits=c(0, 10), breaks=1:10, to = c(0, 15)) +
scale_colour_gradientn(limits = c(0, 10), breaks=1:10, colours = rainbow(7))

However, there seems to be a bug with the legend, which I'm looking into now.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Bubble chart size and colour
parts:
On Mon, Mar 9, 2009 at 7:22 AM, hadley wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Michel,
>
> You need to do the same thing you did with size:  map colour to
> rating, and then find an appropriate scale that performs the mapping
> that you want.  In this case, I'd say you want scale_gradientn which
> allows to you create a mapping to any continuous colour gradient:
>
> ggplot(data = info, aes(lng, lat)) +
> geom_point(aes(size=rating, colour = rating)) +
> scale_size(name='Ratings', limits=c(0, 10), breaks=1:10, to = c(0, 15)) +
> scale_colour_gradientn(limits = c(0, 10), breaks=1:10, colours = rainbow(7))
>
> However, there seems to be a bug with the legend, which I'm looking into now.

scale_area('Ratings', limits=c(0, 10), breaks=1:10, to = c(0, 15)) +
scale_colour_gradientn('Ratings', limits = c(0, 10), breaks=1:10,
colours = rainbow(7))

And you might want to use scale_area instead of scale_size, to make
the area of the points proportional to rating, rather than there
radius.

Hadley
